analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The patch (head lines 2009-2012) updates the reconnect-backoff constants table. It points the backoff row to CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift and adds three rows: a 60 s stable-session reset counted from the register frame, a 0..1 s random wait after close code 1012, and unchanged ping/pong values. The two supplied units (head lines 805-1720) are surrounding unchanged documentation covering Autopilot consent, addon hold, stop/restart, status, doctor, models, benchmark, update, unenroll, logs and refusal lines. I read them as context only; none of that text was modified here.

No security controls, code, endpoints or trust boundaries change. The docs do describe a reconnect policy that touches TB-002 availability. A 1012 reconnect wait of 0..1 s without backoff growth could in principle be abused by a coordinator-side restart storm. The coordinator is trusted, though, and the actual Swift implementation (CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift) is not supplied, so I cannot verify the documented behavior against code. This is a documentation accuracy question and not a demonstrable regression. The provider re-registers and re-attests on each reconnect, so App Attest and legacy authorization (T-053) are unaffected by the delay values.

I found no threat-model gaps from the supplied evidence. The only remaining item for integration is whether the documented constants match CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, which is outside the supplied evidence.
